headline: Regent Hospital's Shahed Karim arrested again in Dhaka
summary: The chairman of Regent Hospital, facing 35 cases including fraud and money laundering, was apprehended by police from the ECB circle area.
details: Police have re-arrested Md. Shahed, also known as Shahed Karim, the chairman of Regent Hospital, from the ECB circle area in Dhaka on Monday afternoon.
The arrest was carried out by Cantonment Police Station, following a request from Pallabi Police Station, as there is an active arrest warrant against him.
Shahed is embroiled in 35 different cases, including charges of fraud, money laundering, and the acquisition of assets beyond known sources of income.
He first gained notoriety during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, when RAB arrested him for issuing fake COVID-19 test reports from Regent Hospital.
According to CID reports, Shahed embezzled over 11 crore BDT, including 3.11 crore BDT earned specifically from the fake COVID-19 certificates.

His legal history is complex: he was sentenced to life imprisonment in an arms act case in 2020, but was later acquitted by the High Court in January 2024, though the verdict was stayed by the Appellate Division.
He had also been sentenced to three years in prison in 2023 for acquiring assets beyond known sources of income and six months in 2010 for check fraud.
caption:

Police have re-arrested Md. Shahed, also known as Shahed Karim, the chairman of Regent Hospital, from the ECB circle area in Dhaka on Monday afternoon.

The arrest was carried out by Cantonment Police Station, following a request from Pallabi Police Station, as there is an active arrest warrant against him.

Shahed is embroiled in 35 different cases, including charges of fraud, money laundering, and the acquisition of assets beyond known sources of income.

He first gained notoriety during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, when RAB arrested him for issuing fake COVID-19 test reports from Regent Hospital.

According to CID reports, Shahed embezzled over 11 crore BDT, including 3.11 crore BDT earned specifically from the fake COVID-19 certificates.

His legal history is complex: he was sentenced to life imprisonment in an arms act case in 2020, but was later acquitted by the High Court in January 2024, though the verdict was stayed by the Appellate Division.

He had also been sentenced to three years in prison in 2023 for acquiring assets beyond known sources of income and six months in 2010 for check fraud.

headline_marked: From 95ft to 15ft: [[Kandi Khal canal shrinks drastically]], causing floods in Comilla
headline: From 95ft to 15ft: Kandi Khal canal shrinks drastically, causing floods in Comilla
summary: Illegal encroachments and unplanned road projects have turned a vital drainage canal into a narrow drain, leaving the city plagued by severe waterlogging.
details: The Kandi Khal, a 5km long canal essential for Comilla city's drainage, has shrunk from its original width of 80-95 feet to just 8-15 feet in many places.
This drastic reduction in size has led to severe waterlogging, forcing HSC candidates to wade through knee-deep or waist-deep water to reach their examination centers on July 13.

Residents report that the canal's capacity was severely compromised when the Comilla-Noakhali regional highway was expanded to four lanes in 2018, which narrowed the canal by nearly half in some areas.
Illegal encroachments by both private individuals and government institutions have further choked the canal with small culverts, steel bridges, and permanent structures.

The Comilla City Corporation (CCC) administrator, Md. Yusuf Molla (Tipu), has warned that any structure obstructing water flow will be demolished, regardless of whether it is owned by a private person or a government entity.

Local history researcher Ahsanul Kabir noted that such severe waterlogging did not exist in the city three decades ago when the canal could efficiently drain water into the Dakatia River via the Gungaijuri Khal.
The Roads and Highways Department (RHD) executive engineer in Comilla, Khandakar Golam Mostafa, has denied that his department occupied any property of the Kandi Khal.
caption:

Residents report that the canal's capacity was severely compromised when the Comilla-Noakhali regional highway was expanded to four lanes in 2018, which narrowed the canal by nearly half in some areas.

Illegal encroachments by both private individuals and government institutions have further choked the canal with small culverts, steel bridges, and permanent structures.

The Comilla City Corporation (CCC) administrator, Md. Yusuf Molla (Tipu), has warned that any structure obstructing water flow will be demolished, regardless of whether it is owned by a private person or a government entity.

Local history researcher Ahsanul Kabir noted that such severe waterlogging did not exist in the city three decades ago when the canal could efficiently drain water into the Dakatia River via the Gungaijuri Khal.

The Roads and Highways Department (RHD) executive engineer in Comilla, Khandakar Golam Mostafa, has denied that his department occupied any property of the Kandi Khal.
